title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The ICSP progamme in Ethiopia has two components. One component will be implemented in the Amhara and SNNPR regions. It focuses on food systems more broadly with the aim of diversifying food production and increasing the supply of nutrient dense foods. 3,000 households (18,000 beneficiaries) will be supported. Communities will be trained in Climate Smart Agriculture and sustainable agriculture techniques. This will include afforestation and tree planting, such as the planting of fruit trees for diversified diet and income. Drought tolerant crop varieties will be used, and irrigation systems established. Training will also be delivered on dietary diversity/nutrition, post harvesting handling, food processing and hygiene. There will be a strong focus on increasing women’s role in decision making particularly in relation to food production. Multi-stakeholder platforms, comprised of government officials and other key stakeholders, will be established and will meet quarterly to discuss issues relating to food security. The programme will also support green technologies such as the use of energy efficient stoves, youth led enterprises for the manufacture of organic fertiliser production/vermi-composting and youth led fruit tree cultivation.The second component of the ICSP programme in Ethiopia focuses specifically on the dairy value chain and will be implemented in Oromia and Amhara regions. 2,000 households (12,000 beneficiaries) will be targeted. The programme will support use of Artificial insemination to enhance the genetics of local breeds and will train Artificial Insemination technicians. Vaccination and treatment will be provided to improve animal health. Nurseries will be established for the supply of seedlings for forage and fodder. Farmers will be trained in backyard forage production and management as well as in enhanced use of crop residues. The programme will support improved access to water supply for dairy cooperative centres and will build the capacity of cooperatives to collectively manage the collection of milk and to conduct milk hygiene testing. Cooperatives will also be trained in cooperative management, marketing, and business plan development and will be linked with local milk processing unions. - A project in Ethiopia supporting a revolving loan fund in savings and credit co-operatives for selected climate smart income generating activities (shoats) commodity to promote green economic growth. Marked 2 for Adaptation.
